hero.description: Global Opportunities brings funding opportunities, calls for projects, applications, evaluation, disbursement and payment tracking into one secure, multilingual workspace. A project owner discovers a call, builds a project against its real criteria, applies, and follows the funding through to delivery — without losing the thread in a dozen inboxes.

trust.title: Built so every step can be checked.
trust.description: Every figure above describes the platform as it is built today. Nothing here is an adoption statistic, because no verified usage data exists yet.
trust.assurance: Security is described by what the platform does — token-based sessions, project-scoped documents, role-based access — not by badges it has not been awarded.

features.title: Everything the journey needs, in one workspace.
features.description: Discovery is where a project owner starts. Everything after it — building the project, applying, being assessed, being funded, being paid, and proving what changed — happens against the same record instead of a new system each time.
details: One searchable index of funding opportunities and calls, filterable by type, sector, location and status.
A structured project record with objectives, results, budget and documents, so the project is built once and reused.
Applications carry a status and a history, so an applicant always knows which stage their submission has reached.
Defined criteria, assigned reviews and a recorded decision, so selection is explainable rather than opaque.
Awarded funding and each disbursement tracked against the project, with the next tranche visible.
Payments recorded against a disbursement, giving both sides one view of what has been paid and what is pending.
Documents uploaded once, categorised, and shared with exactly the parties attached to the project.
Deadline reminders, decision notices and document states delivered to the people who need them.
Plain-language answers about an opportunity, its eligibility and its documents — grounded in official information.

showcase.title: See the workspace before you commit to it.

how.title: Nine stages, one continuous thread.
how.description: Every screen, notification and permission in the platform maps onto one of these nine stages. That is what keeps a project, its application, its funding and its reporting describing the same thing.
details: Search the index of open listings and filter down to the ones that match a sector, a location and a deadline.

Build the project record: objectives, expected results, budget, team and supporting documents.
Submit the project against a listing. The application inherits the project's documents instead of asking again.
Assessments run against defined criteria, with each review recorded against its assignment.
The selection decision is recorded against the application and both parties are notified.
Awarded funding is attached to the project with a disbursement schedule the applicant can see.
Payments are recorded against each disbursement, closing it out as the work is delivered.
Activity, indicators and documents stay visible on the project for its whole life, not just to the deadline.

benefits.title: What changes when the process is in one place.
benefits.description: Most of the friction in applying for funding is not the writing. It is finding the call, working out what it wants, keeping the documents straight, and finding out what happened. These are the eight places the platform removes work.
details: Listings from every provider in one index, with one set of filters, instead of a dozen inboxes and websites.
Documents are attached to the project once and travel with the application, so nothing is re-uploaded per call.
A project is a record with objectives, results, budget and progress, not a folder of differently named files.
Criteria, scores and the decision are visible, so an applicant can see why an application stood or fell.
Awarded funding, the next tranche and what has been paid are visible to both sides at the same time.
Documents are categorised, reviewable and scoped to a project rather than scattered across email.
A user working in Kiswahili reads the same platform as a user working in French, in their own language.
An assistant that explains a call, lists the documents it needs and translates the technical parts.

ecosystem.title: Every actor sees the same record.

testimonials.title: Written around the moments that usually go wrong.
testimonials.notice: Illustrative sample quotes. No user has been quoted yet; replace these with approved, attributed statements before launch.
quotes: I used to keep calls in a spreadsheet that was already out of date. Now the deadline, the documents and where my application sits are all on one page, and I stop working from memory.
We publish a call once and can see every application against the same criteria. Reviewers no longer send us scores by email, and we can answer an applicant's question without hunting for the thread.
I am assigned specific applications, not asked to find them. My scores sit against the published criteria, so the decision I contribute to can be explained to whoever asks.

impact.title: From scattered searching to a trackable process.
items: Stronger links between project owners and funding organisations
impact.description: Five changes, in the order they occur. Each one is a claim about how the platform works rather than a measurement of how well it is working, which is the only kind of claim available before launch.
details: A listing that would have been missed in a crowded inbox is now found with a filter and a deadline alert.
A project assembled against real criteria before the deadline, instead of written at 23:00 the night before.
Funding decisions and disbursements recorded in a place both parties can read, not reconciled from email.
Activity and indicators reviewed on schedule, while the project is still running and can still be adjusted.
Project owners and funding organisations working from the same record instead of exchanging versions.

faq.title: The things people actually ask.
faq.closingLink: Create a free account and read the listings.
faq.description: The twelve questions that decide whether the platform is useful, answered without marketing language. Where the honest answer is that something is not built yet, that is what it says.

a.q1: Two listing types: funding opportunities, which award money against a project, and calls for projects, which invite proposals. Each listing carries a sector, a location, an eligibility summary, the documents it requires and a closing date. The discovery section filters across both types so you can narrow the index before you start reading.
a.q2: Every listing shows a status, and the filter lets you restrict the index to open calls only. The deadline is shown on the card and in the listing detail, and notifications can be configured per user so a closing date is not something you have to remember.
a.q3: A project record with its objectives, budget and documents, plus whatever the specific call asks for. Because documents are attached to the project rather than to the application, a project prepared once can be submitted to several calls without uploading anything again. The AI Assistant will list the documents a call requires.
a.q4: An application has a status and a history rather than a single submitted-or-not flag, so you can see which stage it has reached. Whether a submitted application can still be edited depends on the call's own rules, which are stated in its listing; the platform surfaces the stage, it does not override the funder's policy.
a.q5: Enough to be assessable: what the project will do, for whom, over what period, at what cost, and how you will know it worked. A project is created before a call is applied to, which means you can prepare against real criteria rather than writing to a deadline.
a.q6: Awarded funding is attached to the project together with a disbursement schedule. Each tranche is recorded as it is released, so the applicant can see what has been approved, what has arrived and what is next. The platform records the schedule and its progress; it is not itself a financial institution.
a.q7: The documents a project or call requires — registration certificates, work plans, budgets, concept notes, policies. Every file is categorised and carries a review state, and it is visible to the parties attached to that project rather than being published. Documents are stored against the project record so they stay with it for the project's whole life.
a.q8: Against defined criteria, with each reviewer assigned specific applications and each score recorded against its assignment. The selection decision is stored on the application, which is what makes the outcome explainable to an applicant who asks. The platform does not decide anything itself; it records the criteria, the scores and the decision.
a.q9: Payments are recorded against a disbursement, so a tranche can be reconciled as the work is delivered rather than as one lump at the end. Both the funding provider and the project owner see the same record, which removes the reconciliation that usually happens over email at the end of a reporting period.
a.q10: It explains a listing, summarises eligibility criteria into a checklist, lists the required documents, simplifies dense text, translates an explanation and walks you through the next step of an application. It does not decide funding, does not select applicants, and does not make a final eligibility judgement. Those decisions belong to the people running the call.
a.q11: English, Français, Kirundi and Kiswahili. The selector is in the navbar and the choice is remembered on this device, and it also sets the page's language attribute so screen readers and browser translation work correctly. Interface and page content are translated into all four languages; a listing's own text stays in the language it was written in.
a.q12: Signing in exchanges your credentials for a short-lived access token rather than a stored session, and the platform is built with organisation, evaluator and administrator roles. Documents are scoped to a project instead of being public. Two honest caveats: role enforcement is still being wired into the API's permission classes, and signing out currently clears the token on this device only, because the API has no revocation endpoint yet.
